company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at plus 1.6% versus the consensus of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence in fiscal 2027 growth.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the robotics and AI-driven machine vision market.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid FQ1 EPS beat of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and importantly would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, with adjusted EPS of 42 cents. Sales fell short, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year over year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly while EPS guidance was left unchanged, and FQ2 EPS guidance is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman remaining through the transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership change with no financial results attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year over year to 12.4%, well below the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation straining household budgets through the critical selling season. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost actions, and a roughly 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. The result is a significant positive data point in the highly competitive GLP-1 obesity drug space. This could reprice Viking and create broader read-throughs across the obesity drug sector.

sectors: The RV and discretionary consumer space looks challenged based on THO's commentary around interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation pressuring retail demand. The GLP-1 and obesity drug sector gets a positive jolt from VKTX's 22% weight loss data. Robotics and physical AI get a vote of confidence from CGNX's acquisition of RealSense.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This edition is a pure earnings and company news note for Tuesday September 22, with no macro or rates commentary included. Let's get straight into the names.

Starting with AutoZone. They beat on earnings per share, coming in at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03. But do not get too excited — this was a low-quality beat. The upside was entirely driven by a 145 basis point tailwind from tariff refunds and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Strip those out and the story gets ugly fast. Domestic comps missed badly, up just 1.6% against the Street's 3.1% expectation, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year. Management tried to spin a positive narrative around improving linearity in the back half of the quarter, but the core consumer read here is soft.

THOR Industries is another consumer warning sign. They missed fiscal Q4 earnings per share at 78 cents against the Street's 87 cents. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year over year to 12.4%, well short of the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management's language was cautious — they talked about stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets through the peak selling season. They won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. There were some bright spots — dealer inventory is clean, the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year over year, and structural cost cuts are underway — but the headline is a miss in a tough environment.

On the brighter side, MillerKnoll delivered a genuinely solid quarter. They beat at 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and here's the key — even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund, they still beat at 42 cents. Sales were light, down 3.3% organically, but orders rose 3.5% year over year. Guidance was largely maintained.

Cognex is making a big move into robotics and physical AI, acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception — for roughly $500 million upfront. RealSense is growing revenue more than 50% year over year. This is a strategic bet on the physical AI theme.

And the headline pre-market mover is Viking Therapeutics, spiking after reporting 22% weight loss from its GLP-1 drug VK2735. That is a strong clinical result and puts Viking firmly in the conversation in the obesity drug race.

Directionally, the consumer picture from AutoZone and THOR is cautious. GLP-1 and robotics are the areas with positive momentum this morning. Watch Viking and the broader obesity drug complex for follow-through, and treat AutoZone's beat with skepticism given the quality issues underneath the headline number.
